This was curious one. It fails quickly on Linux but it takes ~30s on my Mac. 

First connect attempt would get RST but there would be subsequent attempt that just hangs long time. 
I'm wondering if this is related to dual mode sockets and fact that `loopback` can resolve to address other than 127.0.0.1 we are binding to. (e.g. ::1)

This all comes from Socket.Connect(DnsEndpoint).

However, this test is trying to verify that the HttpRequestException has the info and that does not really depend on underlying socket operations. I replaced real socket with ConnectCallback that fails immediately and the test takes 0.2s instead of +30s. Since there is no real networking it should be fast and reliable. I removed the OuterLoop label as well. 

fixes #66692

review_comments: This is testing something different now, i.e. an explicitly and synchronously thrown exception at the beginning of initiating a connection vs an exception likely asynchronously coming from the socket layer at some point while failing to connect.  Is that ok?

I think it is OK. The test is looking for something like 
```
  System.Net.Http.HttpRequestException: connection refused (localhost:1234)
```
We added the last part (and this test) in https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/38131

None of this depends on the actual socket error so I feel that would be ok. Since the `ConnectCallback` is ValueTask I can add variation and test the async path as well. 

Perhaps @antonfirsov can comment on this as well since he wrote the test originally.

Let me know if you want me to turn it into Theory with sync & async branch @stephentoub. It was not before but it would not be too difficult to do IMHO. Since both cases are handled by same block as @antonfirsov mentioned, behavior should be the same - unless we change the implementation radically.
It's up to you.  I just wanted to make sure we were aware of the change to what's being validated.
